Write $FF into $EA50 for slot X.
Initialize LEVELI actor type $30 in slot X. Store $02 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Store $FF in $EA50.

Initialize LEVELI actor type $35 in slot X. Store $09 in horizontal extent. Store $10 in vertical extent, horizontal movement. Store $03 in $E9F0. Set the vertical overlap extent at $EA80 and the separate sprite colour at $E930 to five. Store $0F in $E870.
Clear the actor's visibility bit $40.

Initialize LEVELI actor type $34 in slot X. Store $0A in horizontal extent. Store $13 in vertical extent. Store $02 in $E9F0, $EA80. Store $08 in horizontal movement. Set $EB10 to $80 to select direct sprite shapes. Store $0C in sprite colour.
Initialize LEVELI actor type $2F in slot X. Store $0B in horizontal extent. Store $13 in vertical extent. Store $02 in $E9F0, $EA80. Store $0E in sprite colour.
Set extents to two and three and $EA50 to $FF. If the low flag bits are nonzero, keep them in $E840 and clear them in the actor flags.
Set bit $20 in the actor flags and continue at the store in the initializer at $C47F.
Initialize LEVELI actor type $2A in slot X. Apply $20 with OR to actor flags.

Use the random comparison to decide whether to call $2927. Set $E9F0 and $EA80 to three and two and extents ten and eighteen. Set $E870 from two random bits plus four, colour five and direct shape $91. Clear horizontal movement and the counters at $E840, $E9C0 and $E750.
Entry after the optional call to $2927. The timed reset at $C696 enters here to refresh the initialization fields.
Set both extents to three and $EA50 to $FF. Copy nonzero low flag bits to $E840 and clear them.
Write extents three and two, then enter $C411, which overwrites both with three before moving flag bits.
Write extent values two and ten. The common initialization at $C411 then overwrites both with three.
Set colour fourteen, $E9C0 to $14 and bit $10 at $EB10. Set extents sixteen and twenty-one, $EA80 to zero and the fixed address $E9F0 to four.

Initialize LEVELI actor types $2D, $2E, $32 in slot X. Store $01 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Apply $34 with OR to actor flags. Apply $01 with OR to shape and actor flags at $EB10. Store $FF in $EA50. Store $0A in $E870.
Set actor flag $10 and coarse row three, then clear visibility.
Set $E9F0 and $EA80 to two and extents ten and fifteen. Store $FF in $EA50 and clear the visibility flag through $C34C.

Set extents $15 and $26, $E9F0 to three, $EA80 to five and movement to eight. Clear $1D, $1F and $E9C0, call $C511 and allocate three children of types $27 through $29. Give each the parent's coordinates and slot.
Initialize LEVELI actor types $27, $28, $29 in slot X. Store $04 in sprite colour. Store $FF in $EA50. Apply $10 with OR to actor flags.
When $E750 underflows reload it with seven and toggle the low shape bit within the pair selected by direction. Continue to the shared patrol update.

Set movement to $10. Require carry clear from $275A, $E840 zero and success from $2760 with ten. When the random byte is also zero request type $2D through $28AF. Finish with the turn check and four in $08.
Call $287A when the glyph animation phase is zero.
When flag bit $04 is clear, toggle direction bit $08 and set $04. Then run $2757 with four.
Run the resident check and turn logic. When $E750 reaches zero reload it with five, advance the phase modulo four and use the direction group's offset with that phase to read the shape at $C5C1.
Two four-pointer groups indexed by shape phase and direction.
The update callback used by type $2A returns immediately.

Decrement the timer at $C659. When it underflows, reload $0A and advance the phase at $C65A modulo four. Copy 32 bytes backwards into $7988–$79A7, replacing glyphs $31–$34 in the playfield character set.
The four phase offsets $1F, $3F, $5F and $3F point to the last byte of each 32-byte animation frame relative to $C5F9. The copying loop counts down from the selected end.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 0. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $31–$34.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 1 and 3. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $31–$34.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 2. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $31–$34.
Countdown in calls to the stage update. Underflow reloads it with $0A and advances the animation phase.
The update increments this value modulo four and uses it to index the backwards-copy offsets at $C5F5.

Clear horizontal movement, call $275A and advance the shape cycle. When the phase is zero, decrement $E840. A negative result sets movement to $20 and $E840 to two, checks and sets flag $04, then counts down $E870 and may reset the actor.
Call $2927 and refresh the initializer's fields through $C3CC.
On underflow of $E750 reload it to five and decrement phase $E9C0. Use the incoming A when the phase turns negative, then read a shape from the table selected by direction.
Four sprite pointers for the direction with actor flag $08 set.
The alternate direction's four sprite pointers indexed by the same phase.

Advance one coarse row and run $381A when $22E5 sets carry. Remove the actor for $E840 zero. Otherwise use $E840 plus $1A as the new type, remapping $20 to $25 and subtracting nine coarse rows. Call $3854 and clear removal, then test proximity and choose the $27DA argument by relative X.
Call $287A and run $2757 with six, then decrement $E9C0. On underflow reset it to $50 and use the $2760 check to select whether to spawn shots at $C760.
Copy the actor flags and horizontal extent to $7D and $7E. Remove the actor on underflow of $E870. Otherwise continue to $287A.
Allocate four children through $C789. The first two receive opposite vertical movements and the other two horizontal magnitude $40, with the last direction toggled.
Allocate type $2E, give it a timer of ten in $E870 and copy the parent's coordinates.
With $1F set increment colour and make the actor visible. Check each active player unless $1D is negative. Carry from $23D6 calls $216F and removes the actor.

When $1D is nonzero keep its low seven bits in $70 and set $1E to three. Allocate type $2A, set coarse Y of the old slot to nine and copy its position to the new slot. Flag the original for removal, call $3854 on the new slot and set $4F to $FF.

Call $38BD and return while $390C is set. Select colour four or two from $23B7 and run $2757 with six. Carry sets $390C to $14, restores type $26 and clears visibility. Otherwise use the turn logic, test the low four random bits before calling $2838, and spawn three type $32 actors from $C97A when $E9C0 underflows.
Copy the parent's coordinates and add three to coarse X. Then run the shared colour, shape and parent checks.
Copy the parent's coordinates with $0280 added to the two-byte Y coordinate.
Copy the parent's coordinates with three added to coarse X and $0280 added to the two-byte Y coordinate.
Copy the parent shape and colour. Remove the child if $390C is set or the parent's type has changed from $26.
Jump past the parent-flag test to the return.
A zero parent flags byte or a set removal bit sends the child to $2739. Otherwise return.

Take the child type in A and record count in Y. For each five-byte record, add the first two bytes to the parent's coarse coordinates, store the third in $E840 and $E870 and use the last two as movement. Advance the pointer and restore the parent slot in X.
The offset-spawn loop at $C8E3 saves its requested actor type here and reloads it for each allocation.

The twelve five-byte offset records also present at $C66D in LEVELB and $C816 in LEVELD. Fields are coarse offsets, a shared timer byte and two movement bytes. LEVELI's parent update passes the separate group at $C97A to the spawn loop.
Three five-byte records used by the parent actor. Coarse X offsets are two in all three records. The records use timer $64 and horizontal movement $15, with vertical movement $FB, zero and five.
Run $287A and require flag $04. Count $E870 down and remove on underflow. Otherwise retain the flag.
